newsitem.title: USA: Viacom reviewing Blockbuster tracking stock.
newsitem.headline: Viacom reviewing Blockbuster tracking stock.

text.p: Viacom Inc chairman Sumner Redstone said Tuesday the company was reviewing its plans for offering a tracking stock for its Blockbuster video rental unit, according to analysts.
The company said in April it planned an initial public offering of a Blockbuster tracking stock early next year.

But in a conference call with Wall Street analysts, Redstone said the company would not make a decision until Blockbuster's business turned around next year. The company would also consider stock market conditions and the retail environment.
Redstone said the plan was "neither on nor off," according to analysts.
"It's an example of the state of confusion surrounding Blockbuster," said analyst Jill Krutick of Smith Barney.

Analysts said Viacom tried during the call to avoid promising a quick Blockbuster turnaround. "It's very clear the company is focused on under-promising and over-delivering," said Chris Dixon at PaineWebber.
Executives said, for example, that same-store sales would remain negative for the full year.
Viacom took a $323 million charge on Blockbuster in the second quarter.
Tom Dooley, Viacom deputy chairman, said the company does not plan to open any new stores in the fourth quarter and will open 100-150 stores between now and the final period.
Blockbuster ended the quarter with 5,820 stores at June 30.
